problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:

* Component Alpha: size 49 cubic meters
* Component Beta: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Gamma: size 35 cubic meters
* Component Delta: size 36 cubic meters
* Component Epsilon: size 49 cubic meters
* Component Zeta: size 43 cubic meters
* Component Eta: size 31 cubic meters
* Component Theta: size 33 cubic meters
* Component Iota: size 52 cubic meters
* Component Kappa: size 35 cubic meters
* Component Lambda: size 58 cubic meters
* Component Mu: size 48 cubic meters
* Component Nu: size 49 cubic meters
* Component Xi: size 61 cubic meters
* Component Omicron: size 54 cubic meters
* Component Pi: size 47 cubic meters
* Component Rho: size 44 cubic meters
* Component Sigma: size 65 cubic meters
* Component Tau: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Upsilon: size 63 cubic meters
* Component Phi: size 68 cubic meters
* Component Chi: size 36 cubic meters
* Component Psi: size 70 cubic meters
* Component Omega: size 50 cubic meters
* Component Ares: size 55 cubic meters
* Component Zeus: size 53 cubic meters
* Component Hera: size 37 cubic meters
* Component Poseidon: size 64 cubic meters
* Component Apollo: size 39 cubic meters
* Component Athena: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Hermes: size 60 cubic meters
* Component Artemis: size 69 cubic meters
* Component Dionysus: size 67 cubic meters
* Component Hephaestus: size 54 cubic meters
* Component Demeter: size 63 cubic meters
* Component Hestia: size 52 cubic meters
* Component Aphrodite: size 47 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of total shipment volume. Assign all components using the fewest planes possible. Each component must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume assigned to any plane cannot exceed its capacity.
